review.name: National Careers Service
review.graph: Free adviser-led guidance is available to adults in England. Scotland, Wales and NI have their own careers services.
review.note: The text confirms you can get guidance from a careers adviser, but it does not say the service is free, for adults, or limited to England, and it does not mention separate services in Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.
review.quote: Wherever you are with your decisions, you can contact us to get advice from a careers adviser.

review.name: Emergency travel document
review.graph: Must be outside the UK without a valid passport.
review.note: The text requires being outside the UK and unable to use your UK passport for specific listed reasons, some of which (full, or held by HM Passport Office or an embassy) do not mean the passport is invalid, so 'without a valid passport' is only a loose match.
review.quote: your UK passport has been lost, stolen, damaged, is full, has recently expired or is with HM Passport Office or a foreign embassy

review.name: Register as sole trader
review.graph: Has started to trade as a sole trader (self-employed), earning income from their own business.
review.note: The text links registering to trading as a self-employed sole trader, but the stated trigger is earning more than £1,000 in a tax year, which the criterion leaves out, and the text also says you can choose to register earlier.
review.quote: You can start trading straight away without registering. However, you must register for Self Assessment as a sole trader if you earn more than £1,000 in a tax year (from 6 April to 5 April).

review.name: VAT registration
review.graph: Taxable turnover has exceeded or is expected to exceed £90,000 in a rolling 12-month period.
review.note: The £90,000 threshold over the last 12 months is stated, but the text puts the expected-turnover test on the next 30 days, not a rolling 12-month period as the criterion says.
review.quote: your total taxable turnover for the last 12 months goes over £90,000 (the VAT threshold) you expect your taxable turnover to go over £90,000 in the next 30 days

review.name: Report an error with your eVisa
review.graph: Has a UKVI account, including one the Home Office set up that you have never been able to sign in to.
review.note: The text covers the case of an account the Home Office set up that you have never signed in to, but it never says a UKVI account is required for every case, such as reporting wrong eVisa details.
review.quote: the Home Office set up your UKVI account and you’ve never been able to sign in to it

review.name: Immigration fee waiver
review.graph: Must demonstrate that payment of the visa fee would leave you (or your family) destitute or at risk of destitution.
review.note: The text describes not being able to afford the fee because you lack housing or essential living costs, which is close to destitution, but it never says 'destitute' or 'at risk of destitution', and it adds a separate route: very low income where paying would harm your child's wellbeing.
review.quote: You can apply for a fee waiver if you cannot afford to pay the fee because you: do not have a place to live in the UK and you cannot afford one have a place to live but cannot afford essential living costs like food or heating

review.name: Immigration fee waiver
review.graph: Must be applying for a qualifying leave to remain or citizenship application.
review.note: The text supports applications for permission to stay (leave to remain) on certain routes, but it says nothing about citizenship applications.
review.quote: You can apply for a fee waiver if you’re applying for permission to stay in the UK.

review.name: View or prove your immigration status
review.graph: Must have a UKVI account with an eVisa or EU Settlement Scheme status.
review.note: The text says you need a UKVI account and an eVisa, but it never mentions EU Settlement Scheme status as another qualifying route.
review.quote: You’ll need the details you use to sign in to your UKVI account.

review.name: Visa / leave to enter
review.graph: Non-UK, non-Irish national wishing to enter the UK (some nationalities require visa; others may enter visa-free for short stays).
review.note: The text covers people who are not British or Irish and says they may need a visa or an ETA, but it never says outright that some nationalities can enter visa-free for short stays.
review.quote: Check if you need a UK Visa, electronic travel authorisation (ETA) or get access to an eVisa to prove your immigration status if you’re not a British citizen or Irish national

review.name: Visa / leave to enter
review.graph: Must apply for the specific visa type matching the purpose of entry (Skilled Worker, Student, Family Visa, etc.).
review.note: The text groups visa types by purpose (work, study, family) and names Skilled Worker and Student visas, but it does not say you must apply for the visa that matches your purpose of entry.
review.quote: Work in the UK Skilled Worker visa, Graduate visa, other work visas, right to work Study in the UK Student visas

review.name: Apply for bankruptcy
review.graph: Must live or have a business in England or Wales.
review.note: The text limits the service to England and Wales but does not say the applicant must live or have a business there.
review.quote: Use this service to apply for bankruptcy in England and Wales.

review.name: Apply for a proxy vote
review.graph: Typical reasons include being at work, abroad, or unable to attend due to disability or illness.
review.note: The text gives the general reason (you cannot go to the polling station) and covers applicants who live abroad, but it never names being at work, disability or illness as reasons.
review.quote: You can get someone else to vote on your behalf (a proxy) if you cannot go to the polling station in person.

review.name: Street trading licence
review.graph: Selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales.
review.note: The text covers trading in the street in England and Wales, but it never mentions a 'public place' or says 'goods or services'.
review.quote: You may need to get a licence to trade in the street in England and Wales

review.name: Sign your mortgage deed
review.graph: Lender must participate in the Land Registry digital mortgage service.
review.note: The text says lenders can use HM Land Registry's digital mortgage service, but it never says the homeowner's lender must take part for the homeowner to be eligible.
review.quote: Lenders and conveyancers can use the service to create and register legal mortgages of residential property for homeowners who are remortgaging.

review.name: NHS Continuing Healthcare (CHC)
review.graph: Primary health need assessed as complex, intense, or unpredictable — usually a progressive serious illness, terminal condition, or severe disability.
review.note: The text requires a primary health need arising from disability, accident or illness, but it does not describe that need as complex, intense or unpredictable, and it does not mention progressive serious illness or terminal conditions.
review.quote: arranged and funded solely by the NHS where an individual is found to have a primary health need

review.name: Healthy Start
review.graph: England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scotland has Best Start Foods instead.
review.note: The text says Scotland has Best Start Foods instead, but it never says the scheme covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
review.quote: If you live in Scotland You can get help from Best Start Foods (opens in a new tab) instead.

review.name: Prescription Prepayment Certificate (PPC)
review.graph: Only worthwhile if you pay for NHS prescriptions — exempt groups should not apply.
review.note: The text presents the PPC as a way to cut the cost of prescriptions you pay for, but it does not mention exempt groups or say they should not apply.
review.quote: You can buy prescription prepayment certificates ( PPCs ) from the NHS which may make your prescriptions cheaper.

review.name: Prescription Prepayment Certificate (PPC)
review.graph: England only — prescriptions are free in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
review.note: The England-only restriction is stated, but the text does not say prescriptions are free in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
review.quote: You can only get a PPC if you live in England.

review.name: Raise concerns about a school with Ofsted
review.graph: Must have first completed the school's own complaints procedure before escalating to Ofsted.
review.note: The text says you must already have complained to the school and the problem is still unresolved, but it never says the school's full complaints procedure has to be completed first.
review.quote: you’ve complained to the school and the problem has not been resolved

review.name: Motability scheme
review.graph: Receiving the Enhanced Rate of the Mobility Component of PIP (or equivalent: DLA highest rate mobility, AFIP or WPMS).
review.note: The text mentions only a 'qualifying mobility allowance'. It does not name the PIP enhanced mobility rate, DLA higher rate mobility, AFIP or WPMS.
review.quote: Use your qualifying mobility allowance to lease a brand-new vehicle.

review.name: Pupil Premium
review.graph: Free School Meals eligibility must be registered — the school receives the funding automatically.
review.note: The text bases funding on pupils recorded as FSM-eligible in the school census, with DfE or the local authority allocating it, but it never says families must register FSM eligibility or that the school gets the money automatically.
review.quote: DfE will allocate PP grant to academies directly. This allocation will be based on FSM Ever 6 pupils, PLAC and eligible service children.

review.name: Check and challenge business rates
review.graph: Must occupy or own a non-domestic property assessed for business rates in England.
review.note: The text covers properties in England or Wales that have a rateable value for business rates and refers to 'your property', but it never says you must occupy or own the property, and it never limits the service to England or to non-domestic property.
review.quote: If you want to report a change to your property or challenge its rateable value, use your business rates valuation account .

review.name: ACAS early conciliation
review.graph: Must have an employment dispute such as unfair dismissal, discrimination, unpaid wages or unlawful deduction.
review.note: The text gives unfair dismissal, pay and wages, and discrimination as claim types, but it never mentions unlawful deduction.
review.quote: unfair dismissal – the time limit starts from the 'effective date of termination'.

review.name: Close a limited company
review.graph: Must be a director of a UK limited company that has not traded or otherwise been used for a purpose in the past 3 months.
review.note: The text supports the 3-month no-trading condition, but it says nothing about the company being 'otherwise used for a purpose' or about it having to be a UK company.
review.quote: has not traded or sold off any stock in the last 3 months

review.name: File a confirmation statement
review.graph: Must be a registered company, LLP or eligible UK business entity.
review.note: The text says a company must file, but it never mentions LLPs or other eligible UK business entities, and it states no eligibility rule.
review.quote: You need to check that the information Companies House has about your company is correct every year. This is called a confirmation statement.

review.name: Register limited company (IN01)
review.graph: Registered office must be in England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland. No nationality restriction on directors or shareholders.
review.note: The text requires a UK registered office and says directors need not live in the UK, but it never addresses nationality for directors or shareholders.
review.quote: Directors do not have to live in the UK but companies must have a UK registered office address.

review.name: Apply for teacher training
review.graph: Must have, or be working towards, a UK undergraduate degree (2:2 or above).
review.note: The text asks for a degree or an equivalent, but it does not say the degree must be from the UK, give a 2:2 minimum, or mention people still working towards a degree.
review.quote: You need the following or equivalents: a degree

review.name: Care to Learn
review.graph: Parent must be under 20 at the start of the academic year.
review.note: The age limit of under 20 matches, but the source measures it at the start of the course, not the academic year.
review.quote: You must be aged under 20 at the start of your course.

review.name: Cancel driving licence
review.graph: Person with a GB driving licence has died.
review.note: The text covers a driver or licence holder who has died but never says 'GB' licence; it only says Northern Ireland has a different process.
review.quote: Write to DVLA to tell them a driver has died.

review.name: View and share driving licence
review.graph: Must hold a UK driving licence.
review.note: The text limits the service to licences issued in England, Wales or Scotland, which is narrower than any UK driving licence.
review.quote: if your licence was issued in England, Wales or Scotland

review.name: Update driving licence (name change)
review.graph: Has legally changed name following marriage, civil partnership, deed poll or court order.
review.note: Marriage, civil partnership and deed poll are listed as evidence, but a court order is not mentioned and no 'legal change' condition is stated.
review.quote: your marriage or civil partnership certificate (if you’ve changed your surname)

review.name: Provisional Driving Licence
review.graph: Must be at least 15 years and 9 months old to apply. Must be 17 to drive on a public road (16 for a moped or light quad bike).
review.note: The application age is stated, but the driving ages of 17 and 16 are not; the text only says the rules depend on age and vehicle.
review.quote: be at least 15 years and 9 months old

review.name: Provisional Driving Licence
review.graph: Must have been resident in Great Britain for at least 185 days in the last 12 months.
review.note: The text gives 185 days of permission to live in Great Britain, but it does not mention 'the last 12 months'.
review.quote: have been given permission to live in Great Britain (England, Scotland and Wales) for at least 185 days

review.name: Provisional Driving Licence
review.graph: Must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres away (with glasses or contact lenses if worn). Certain medical conditions must be declared.
review.note: The number plate rule with glasses or contact lenses is stated, but the only declaration duty in the text covers certain eyesight problems, not medical conditions in general.
review.quote: You must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres away (about the length of 5 parked cars). You can wear your glasses or contact lenses if you use them for driving.

review.name: Renew driving licence at 70
review.graph: Must confirm at renewal that eyesight meets minimum standard and no medical condition prevents driving. DVLA may require medical evidence if a condition has been declared.
review.note: The text states the eyesight and fitness conditions and says DVLA may test your eyesight after a reported vision condition, but it does not say you must confirm these things, or that medical evidence may be required for any declared condition.
review.quote: If you report a medical condition that affects your vision, DVLA may refer you for an eyesight test with their contracted optician.

review.name: Renew driving licence
review.graph: Must hold a valid UK driving licence. Photo expiry renewal applies every 10 years for drivers under 70.
review.note: The 10-year renewal and the separate route for people 70 or over are stated, but the listed requirements are living in Great Britain and not being disqualified; holding a valid UK licence isn't stated as a requirement.
review.quote: You must renew a photocard licence every 10 years

review.name: Make a SORN
review.graph: Registered keeper of a vehicle whose tax has lapsed or is about to lapse, and which will be kept off public roads.
review.note: The source ties online applications to vehicles registered in your name and covers off-road use, but it does not limit SORN to vehicles whose tax has lapsed or is about to. It allows applying in other months too, and the post route covers vehicles not registered in your name.
review.quote: You can apply online if the vehicle is registered in your name.

review.name: Tax your vehicle
review.graph: Must have a V5C log book in your name (or the green new keeper slip if recently purchased), a valid MOT, and valid insurance before taxing.
review.note: The V5C or green slip is stated, but a reminder letter reference is also accepted, the MOT is only something you 'might' need, and insurance is only required in Northern Ireland.
review.quote: You might also need to show evidence of an MOT (it must be valid when the tax starts).

review.name: Driving Test (practical)
review.graph: A valid theory test pass certificate (valid for 2 years from the date of the theory test) is required to book.
review.note: You must have passed the theory test, but the source gives no 2-year validity and says you do not need a replacement certificate if you lose it.
review.quote: You must usually have passed your theory test before booking.

review.name: Attendance Allowance
review.graph: Must have reached State Pension age (66 or over).
review.note: The text requires State Pension age but never gives the age 66.
review.quote: You can get Attendance Allowance if you’ve reached State Pension age

review.name: Repay a benefit overpayment
review.graph: Must have been notified by DWP of a benefit overpayment.
review.note: The text says you'll get a letter, but it doesn't make being notified a requirement. It even tells you to report an overpayment yourself if you think you're being overpaid.
review.quote: You’ll get a letter to let you know that you’ve been overpaid.

review.name: Bereavement Support Payment
review.graph: Must have been under State Pension age (66) at the time of the partner's death.
review.note: The source says under State Pension age but does not give the age as 66.
review.quote: When your partner died, you must have been: under State Pension age

review.name: Bereavement Support Payment
review.graph: Deceased must have paid at least 25 weeks of Class 1 or 2 NI contributions, or died from a work-related accident or disease.
review.note: The source says 'a certain amount' of contributions and does not give a figure of 25 weeks; the work accident or disease alternative is stated.
review.quote: paid a certain amount of Class 1 or Class 2 National Insurance contributions in any one tax year since 6 April 1975 died because of an accident at work or a disease caused by work

review.name: Disability Living Allowance (Child)
review.graph: Must be in England, Wales or Northern Ireland (Scotland uses Child Disability Payment).
review.note: England, Wales and the Scotland exclusion are stated, but Northern Ireland families are sent to a separate 'DLA for children in Northern Ireland' application rather than being covered by this service.
review.quote: be living in England or Wales when you claim (unless you’re eligible to claim from abroad)

review.name: Funeral Expenses Payment
review.graph: You or your partner must be receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Income Support, income-based JSA, income-related ESA, Housing Benefit, or the child tax credit and working tax credit element at the maximum rate.
review.note: UC, income-related ESA, Pension Credit and Housing Benefit are listed, but Income Support, income-based JSA and tax credits are not in the text.
review.quote: You (or your partner) must get one or more of the following: Universal Credit income-related Employment and Support Allowance Pension Credit Housing Benefit

review.name: Funeral Expenses Payment
review.graph: You are responsible for the funeral costs of a partner, close relative, or close friend where there is no other close relative able to pay.
review.note: The text covers partners and close relatives or friends, but its conditions are about the deceased having no partner or the partner being unable to claim, and a close relative who is working or not on a qualifying benefit may stop you getting the payment. It does not say 'no other close relative able to pay'.
review.quote: If you’re a close relative or friend You might be able to get a Funeral Expenses Payment if: the deceased did not have a partner when they died the partner of the deceased or parent of a deceased child cannot claim

review.name: Mandatory Reconsideration
review.graph: A DWP benefit decision has been received (e.g. UC, JSA, ESA, PIP award or change). Mandatory Reconsideration must happen before a tribunal appeal.
review.note: The text covers these benefits and says the notice comes before an appeal, but it never names DWP and it says some decisions can go straight to an appeal.
review.quote: You cannot appeal to the Social Security and Child Support Tribunal until you get your mandatory reconsideration notice.

review.name: New Style ESA
review.graph: Must have paid sufficient Class 1 or Class 2 NI contributions in both of the last two complete tax years.
review.note: The text requires enough NI contributions 'usually in the last 2 to 3 years' and says credits count; it names no Class 1 or Class 2 contributions and no 'both of the last two complete tax years' rule.
review.quote: paid enough National Insurance contributions, usually in the last 2 to 3 years - National Insurance credits also count

review.name: New Style Jobseeker's Allowance
review.graph: Must have paid Class 1 NI contributions in both of the last two complete tax years before the year of claim.
review.note: The text says Class 1 contributions for the previous 2 tax years are usually needed, but it also says credits can count for one of those years, so it does not say you must have paid in both years.
review.quote: To be eligible you must usually have made Class 1 National Insurance contributions for the previous 2 tax years. National Insurance credits can count for one of these years if you did not pay National Insurance contributions.

review.name: National Insurance number
review.graph: Must have the right to work in the UK, evidenced by a Biometric Residence Permit, eVisa, or other valid leave to remain.
review.note: The right to work is stated, but the text never says it must be shown with a BRP, eVisa or other leave to remain.
review.quote: you must have the right to live and work in the UK

review.name: National Insurance number
review.graph: UK citizens are automatically assigned one — applies mainly to non-UK nationals who have arrived to work or study.
review.note: Automatic issue is only described for UK residents where a Child Benefit claim was made, not for all UK citizens, and the text never says the service is mainly for non-UK nationals arriving to work or study.
review.quote: You’ll normally be sent a National Insurance number in the 3 months before your 16th birthday if both the following are true: you live in the UK a parent or guardian has filled in a Child Benefit claim form for you

review.name: Pension Credit
review.graph: Must have reached State Pension age (currently 66).
review.note: The source says you must have reached State Pension age but does not say it is currently 66.
review.quote: have reached State Pension age to qualify for Pension Credit

review.name: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
review.graph: Must be aged 16 to 64 (under State Pension age). Those over 65 who did not have PIP before should claim Attendance Allowance instead.
review.note: The text gives State Pension age, not 64 or 65, and makes the exception people who got PIP or ADP in the last 12 months, not anyone who ever had PIP.
review.quote: If you’re over State Pension age , you cannot usually make a new claim for PIP . You can apply for Attendance Allowance instead.

review.name: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
review.graph: Long-term physical or mental health condition or disability affecting daily living or mobility. Must have had difficulties for at least 3 months and expect them to continue for at least 9 months.
review.note: The condition requirement is stated, but the text gives a single 12-month expectation and never mentions a 3-month qualifying period or a 9-month future period.
review.quote: you expect the difficulties to last for at least 12 months from when they started

review.name: Support for Mortgage Interest
review.graph: Must be a homeowner with a mortgage, loan or other charge on the property.
review.note: A mortgage or home improvement loan is required, but the text never mentions an 'other charge' on the property.
review.quote: you must have a mortgage or home improvement loan for the property you live in

review.name: State Pension claim
review.graph: Must have reached State Pension age (currently 66 for men and women).
review.note: The text says you must reach State Pension age but never says that age is 66.
review.quote: You’ll be able to claim the new State Pension when you reach State Pension age

review.name: State Pension claim
review.graph: Need at least 10 qualifying years of NI contributions or credits to receive any State Pension; 35 years for the full amount.
review.note: The 10-year minimum, counting contributions or credits, is stated. But 35 years for the full amount applies only to records that started after April 2016; contracted-out people usually need more than 35.
review.quote: If you were contracted out, you will usually need more than 35 qualifying years to get the full rate of new State Pension.

review.name: Tell Us Once
review.graph: Death registered in England, Scotland or most of Wales (not available in all areas).
review.note: The text ties eligibility to where the person lived (England, Scotland or Wales) and to the death being registered or reported to a coroner; it does not say 'most of Wales' or that some areas are excluded.
review.quote: You can use Tell Us Once if the person who died was living in England, Scotland or Wales.

review.name: UC Carer element
review.graph: Eligible for Carer's Allowance (caring 35+ hours/week for someone on qualifying disability benefit).
review.note: The source supports caring 35+ hours a week for someone on a listed benefit, but does not frame this as Carer's Allowance eligibility.
review.quote: You need to provide care for them for at least 35 hours a week.

review.name: UC limited capability element
review.graph: Health condition or disability that limits or prevents capacity for work, determined by a Work Capability Assessment.
review.note: The text states the health condition requirement, but does not say a Work Capability Assessment decides it for this element.
review.quote: You might get an extra monthly amount if you cannot work because of a health condition, disability or long-term illness.

review.name: Universal Credit
review.graph: Must be habitually resident in the UK.
review.note: The text requires living in the UK but does not mention a habitual residence test.
review.quote: To claim you must: live in the UK

review.name: Voluntary National Insurance contributions (Class 3)
review.graph: You have gaps in your National Insurance record that would increase your State Pension if filled.
review.note: The text requires gaps and tells you to check whether paying will help, but it does not make an increase to your pension a condition of paying.
review.quote: You cannot pay voluntary contributions if you: do not have gaps in your National Insurance record

review.name: Voluntary National Insurance contributions (Class 3)
review.graph: Under State Pension age, or within the window where contributions still count.
review.note: The 6-year deadline window is stated, but the text does not require you to be under State Pension age: people over it can pay Class 3.
review.quote: If you've reached State Pension age and want to fill in gaps in your National Insurance record you can pay: Class 3 contributions

review.name: Winter Fuel Payment
review.graph: Must usually live in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, and be there in the qualifying week of 21 to 27 September 2026.
review.note: Usual residence and the qualifying week dates are stated, but the text never says you must be physically present in England, Wales or Northern Ireland during the qualifying week.
review.quote: were visiting England, Wales or Northern Ireland on 21 to 27 September 2026 (the ‘qualifying week’), but usually live somewhere else

review.name: Obtain death certificates
review.graph: Death must have been registered before certified copies can be ordered.
review.note: The text refers to registered deaths but never states registration as a condition for ordering copies.
review.quote: All births, adoptions, marriages, civil partnerships and deaths registered in England or Wales have a GRO index reference number.

review.name: Give notice of marriage
review.graph: Both parties must be 18 or over (16-17 with parental consent in exceptional circumstances).
review.note: The text supports the rule of 18 or over, but says nothing about 16-17 year olds marrying with parental consent.
review.quote: You can get married or form a civil partnership in England or Wales if you’re: 18 or over

review.name: Marriage / CP certificate
review.graph: Must have legally married or formed a civil partnership in England or Wales.
review.note: The service covers certificates registered in England and Wales, but a linked page says GRO also holds some marriage records from abroad, so the text doesn't set a strict England-or-Wales requirement.
review.quote: There’s a different process for getting certificates in Scotland and getting certificates in Northern Ireland .

review.name: Register the birth
review.graph: Deadline is 42 days in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and 21 days in Scotland.
review.note: The source supports the 42-day deadline but gives no 21-day deadline for Scotland.
review.quote: All births in England, Wales and Northern Ireland must be registered within 42 days of the child being born.

review.name: Social Security & Child Support Tribunal
review.graph: Mandatory Reconsideration must have been completed and the outcome confirmed in a Mandatory Reconsideration Notice from DWP.
review.note: The linked page supports needing the notice, but the main page says some people can appeal straight away without reconsideration, and DWP is never named.
review.quote: You cannot appeal to the Social Security and Child Support Tribunal until you get your mandatory reconsideration notice.

review.name: Divorce application (D8)
review.graph: Must have been married or in a civil partnership for at least 1 year.
review.note: The divorce page says you must have been married for over a year; the civil partnership condition comes from a linked page about a different service.
review.quote: you’ve been married for over a year

review.name: Employment Tribunal claim
review.graph: Must have an employment dispute — unfair dismissal requires at least 2 years' service; discrimination claims have no service requirement.
review.note: The linked dismissal page gives the normal 2-year period for unfair dismissal, but the text never says discrimination claims have no service requirement.
review.quote: You must be classed as an employee and have worked for your employer for a minimum period - normally 2 years - before you qualify for the right to claim unfair dismissal at a tribunal.

review.name: Employment Tribunal claim
review.graph: Must have an Acas EC certificate (early conciliation must be attempted first).
review.note: The text says a certificate is usually needed and lists exceptions; it also says you can choose not to take part in conciliation, so conciliation does not have to be attempted.
review.quote: You’ll usually need an early conciliation certificate for each respondent before you make a claim .

review.name: Legal Aid application
review.graph: Disposable income must be below £2,657/month and disposable capital below £8,000 (thresholds vary by case type).
review.note: The figures match, but the text describes £2,657 as joint gross income (before deductions), not disposable income, and says nothing about thresholds varying by case type.
review.quote: have a joint monthly income of £2,657 or less (before tax and other deductions)

review.name: Apply for probate
review.graph: Person has died leaving assets held in their sole name.
review.note: The text refers to a person who has died and suggests jointly owned assets may not need probate, but it never mentions 'sole name' or makes this a stated condition.
review.quote: You may not need probate if the person who died: only had savings owned shares or money with others

review.name: Cancel Marriage Allowance
review.graph: Previously claimed Marriage Allowance and relationship has now ended (separated, divorced, or partner died).
review.note: Divorce, dissolution and legal separation are stated reasons to cancel, but a partner's death is not. The text treats death separately, describing how the allowances change rather than calling for cancellation.
review.quote: your relationship ends - because you’ve divorced, ended (‘dissolved’) your civil partnership or legally separated

review.name: Carer's Credit
review.graph: Not already receiving NI credits through Carer's Allowance, UC, or earnings above the Lower Earnings Limit.
review.note: The Carer's Credit page does not mention Universal Credit, and the linked Carer's Allowance page only says UC gives Class 3 credits, without linking that to Carer's Credit eligibility.

review.name: Child Benefit transfer
review.graph: Child has moved to live primarily with a different parent after separation.
review.note: The text links entitlement to living with the child, but it does not name a child moving to the other parent after separation as a condition for this service.
review.quote: You'll usually be responsible for a child if either: you live with them

review.name: Child Benefit transfer
review.graph: Parents have separated and current Child Benefit claimant is no longer the main carer.
review.note: The text covers families splitting up, but it never says the current claimant no longer being the main carer is a condition for changing who gets Child Benefit.
review.quote: If a family splits up, you get £27.05 a week for the eldest child.

review.name: Register for Corporation Tax
review.graph: All UK-registered limited companies, regardless of profitability or size.
review.note: The text covers limited companies, but only those that are active and within the charge to Corporation Tax. It says nothing about profitability or size.
review.quote: if your limited company is within the charge of Corporation Tax and is now active

review.name: Register for Corporation Tax
review.graph: Requires Companies House registration to be in place first.
review.note: The written application asks for the company's registration number, which suggests the company is already registered, but the text never says Companies House registration must come first.
review.quote: the company’s name and registration number

review.name: Marriage Allowance
review.graph: One partner must have income below the Personal Allowance (£12,570/year). The other must be a basic-rate (20%) taxpayer.
review.note: The source supports the income limit and the basic-rate requirement, but it also allows starter or intermediate rate in Scotland, and the field leaves out that condition.
review.quote: If you're in Scotland, your partner must pay the starter, basic or intermediate rate, which usually means their income is between £12,571 and £43,662.

review.name: Making Tax Digital enrolment
review.graph: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Phased in for income tax self-assessment from 2026.
review.note: The VAT part is supported, apart from exemptions; the income tax self-assessment rollout from 2026 is not stated.
review.quote: All VAT registered businesses should now be signed up for Making Tax Digital for VAT.

review.name: Obtain P45 from employer
review.graph: Must have been employed under PAYE and left that employment.
review.note: The text says you must be an employee who stops working for the employer, but the page text never mentions PAYE.
review.quote: You’ll only get these forms if you’re an employee .

review.name: Stamp Duty Land Tax return
review.graph: Any purchase of land or property in England (or Northern Ireland) — thresholds vary for first-time buyers, additional properties, etc.
review.note: The text confirms England and Northern Ireland and a different threshold for first-time buyers, but for additional properties it describes a 5% higher rate rather than a different threshold, and it lists exemptions (for example freeholds under £40,000) where neither tax nor a return is needed, so not every purchase is covered.
review.quote: SDLT starts to apply when you buy property that costs: £125,000 for residential properties £300,000 for first-time buyers buying a residential property worth £500,000 or less

review.name: Shared Parental Leave & Pay
review.graph: Mother must be eligible for SMP or Maternity Allowance for SPL to be available.
review.note: The text requires maternity leave and pay (or Maternity Allowance) to be cut short, but it never says the mother must be eligible for SMP or Maternity Allowance. Where the partner takes SPL, the mother's criteria are about work and earnings instead.
review.quote: take less than the 39 weeks of maternity or adoption pay (or Maternity Allowance) and use the rest as ShPP

review.name: Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)
review.graph: Must be classed as an employee (including agency workers) and have done some work for the employer; self-employed individuals are not eligible.
review.note: Being classed as an employee and having done some work are stated, and Source 2 says self-employed people lack employee rights. But agency workers only 'may be entitled', so the text does not say they are included outright.
review.quote: Agency workers may be entitled to Statutory Sick Pay .

review.name: Tax-Free Childcare account
review.graph: Provider must be approved childcare and signed up to Tax-Free Childcare. Check registration with Ofsted or a registered childminder agency in England, Care Inspectorate Wales, the Care Inspectorate in Scotland, or the local early years team in Northern Ireland.
review.note: The text tells you to check the provider is registered but does not name any of these bodies.
review.quote: Check if your childcare provider is registered .

review.name: Biometric Residence Permit
review.graph: Granted a UK visa or leave to remain for more than 6 months.
review.note: The text links holding a BRP to being granted permission to live or work in the UK, but it gives no 'more than 6 months' length and instead names a cut-off date of 31 October 2024.
review.quote: You might have a BRP if you were granted permission to live or work in the UK on or before 31 October 2024.

review.name: British citizenship (naturalisation)
review.graph: Must be of good character (no serious criminal record) and demonstrate knowledge of English, Welsh or Scottish Gaelic.
review.note: The source states good character and the language requirement, but it does not define good character as having no serious criminal record.
review.quote: prove your knowledge of English , Welsh or Scottish Gaelic have passed the life in the UK test intend to continue living in the UK be of good character

review.name: Citizenship ceremony
review.graph: Adults aged 18 and over must attend in person. Children under 18 can be included on a parent's ceremony.
review.note: The text says people aged 18 or over must attend, but it never says 'in person' and says nothing about adding children under 18 to a parent's ceremony.
review.quote: You need to attend a citizenship ceremony if you’re 18 or over and have successfully applied to become a British citizen.

review.name: Life in the UK test
review.graph: Applying for Indefinite Leave to Remain or British citizenship (by naturalisation, as spouse/civil partner of a British citizen, or as an Irish citizen).
review.note: The source says the test is part of citizenship or settlement applications, but it does not link the test to the specific routes named (naturalisation, spouse/civil partner, Irish citizen).
review.quote: You need to take the test as part of your application for British citizenship or settlement in the UK.

review.name: Breathing Space (debt respite scheme)
review.graph: Must engage with an FCA-authorised debt advice provider who applies on the person's behalf.
review.note: The text says a debt adviser applies on the person's behalf, but for Breathing Space it does not say the adviser must be FCA-authorised.
review.quote: To apply for the ‘Breathing Space’ scheme, you need to talk to a debt adviser. They will submit an application on your behalf if it’s the right thing to do.

review.name: Free bus pass
review.graph: Must have reached State Pension age (currently 66). Some disabled people may also qualify before this age.
review.note: The text supports State Pension age, and it supports some people getting the pass sooner ('check if you can get one sooner', plus the disabled pass), but it never gives the figure 66.
review.quote: In England you can get a bus pass for free travel when you reach the State Pension age .

review.name: Carer's Assessment
review.graph: Any adult (18+) who provides regular and substantial unpaid care for someone with a disability, health condition, or frailty.
review.note: The text supports being over 18 and caring regularly for someone who is ill, older or disabled, but it does not say the care must be 'substantial' or 'unpaid'.
review.quote: You're a carer if you're looking after someone regularly because they're ill, they're an older person or they're disabled

review.name: Child performance licence
review.graph: Applies in England, Scotland and Wales; Northern Ireland has separate rules.
review.note: The text confirms Northern Ireland has different rules but never names England, Scotland and Wales as the places where this applies.
review.quote: The rules are different in Northern Ireland .

review.name: Council Tax Disability Reduction
review.graph: Property must have at least one of: a room mainly used by the disabled person (not a bedroom, bathroom or kitchen); an extra bathroom or kitchen for the disabled person; extra space inside for wheelchair use.
review.note: The text supports the extra bathroom or kitchen, an other room, and wheelchair space, but it does not say the room must be mainly used by the disabled person or that bedrooms are excluded.
review.quote: You’ll have to show that you have either: an extra bathroom, kitchen or other room that you need for the disabled person extra space inside the property for using a wheelchair

review.name: Council Tax Reduction
review.graph: Low income or receiving means-tested benefits such as Universal Credit, Income Support, Pension Credit.
review.note: The text mentions low income and claiming benefits, but it does not name Universal Credit, Income Support or Pension Credit, and does not say the benefits must be means-tested.
review.quote: You could be eligible if you’re on a low income or claim benefits.

review.name: Council Tax single person discount
review.graph: Now living alone as the only adult (18+) in the property, following bereavement or separation.
review.note: The text supports living on your own and says you usually pay Council Tax from age 18, but it never mentions bereavement or separation.
review.quote: You’ll get 25% off your bill if you pay Council Tax and either: you live on your own

review.name: Disabled Facilities Grant
review.graph: Property in England where the disabled person lives, whether owned, rented privately, or from a housing association.
review.note: Owners, tenants and landlords can apply, and the disabled person must intend to live there. Housing associations are not mentioned, and the grant is not limited to England: Wales and Northern Ireland are also covered.
review.quote: The person who submits the application must be either the: owner tenant landlord

review.name: Electoral roll update
review.graph: Must be 16 or over to register (18 to vote in most elections).
review.note: The minimum age of 16 applies only in England and Northern Ireland (it is 14 in Scotland and Wales), and the text gives 18 only for particular elections, such as general elections, not as a rule for most elections.
review.quote: If you live in England or Northern Ireland You must be aged 16 or over to register.

review.name: Electoral roll update
review.graph: British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen (EU citizens can vote in local elections).
review.note: The text supports British, Irish and Commonwealth citizens (Commonwealth only with permission to enter or stay), but in England and Northern Ireland only certain EU citizens can vote in local elections: those from named countries, or those with continuous permission since 31 December 2020.
review.quote: You can register to vote if you're a British citizen or an Irish citizen. You can also register if you have permission (or do not need permission) to enter or stay in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man and you're: a Commonwealth citizen

review.name: Public film or TV screening permissions
review.graph: Showing films or TV programmes in a public or communal setting: cinema club, hotel, pub, outdoor event, community hall, retail display, or staff room.
review.note: The text lists staff rooms, hotels, retail venues, film clubs and one-off events, but does not name pubs, outdoor events or community halls.
review.quote: Public spaces or events may include: staff rooms common areas for guests or passengers (for example receptions or lounge spaces) bedrooms in hotels and guesthouses retail and entertainment venues one-off events film clubs community cinemas

review.name: School place application
review.graph: Local authority area determines which schools are offered. Catchment area, siblings, faith criteria vary by school.
review.note: The text supports criteria varying by school, including siblings, faith and living close by, but it does not say the local authority area determines which schools are offered (you can apply for schools in other council areas), and it never mentions catchment areas.
review.quote: Admission criteria are different for each school. They may give priority to children: who live close to the school who have a brother or sister at the school already from a particular religion (for faith schools)

review.name: Short-term let licence (Scotland)
review.graph: Must own or manage a residential property being let for short-term stays.
review.note: The text links the licence to letting out accommodation to temporary guests, but it never says you must own or manage the property or that the property must be residential.
review.quote: You may need a short-term let licence if you’re letting out accommodation to guests who stay temporarily.

review.name: Voter Authority Certificate
review.graph: Must be eligible to vote (registered on the electoral roll as a British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen).
review.note: Registration is required, but the text never ties this service to the listed nationalities (and the register page lets other nationalities register too).
review.quote: You must be registered to vote to apply.

review.name: Voter Authority Certificate
review.graph: Must be registered to vote. Only needed if you do not already have an accepted form of photo ID.
review.note: Registration is required, but the text gives other reasons to apply as well (you no longer look like your photo, or your name is different), and it applies only to voting in person.
review.quote: You only need to apply for a Voter Authority Certificate if you vote in person and: you do not have accepted photo ID you no longer look like the photo on your ID the name on your photo ID is different

review.name: Land Registry registration (AP1)
review.graph: Any purchase of land or property in England or Wales. Also required for remortgages, transfers of equity, and first-time registrations of unregistered land.
review.note: The text covers buying, mortgaging, adding a joint owner and first registration, but 'any purchase' leaves out the short-lease exemption.
review.quote: You do not usually need to register leasehold land or property if there are 7 years or less on the lease when you take ownership.

review.name: Send a fit note for an ESA claim
review.graph: Must have a health condition or disability that prevents or limits work, evidenced by a fit note from a healthcare provider.
review.note: The linked ESA page links a fit note to a disability or health condition that stops you working, but only when you have been off work for more than 7 days in a row, and the fit note page says you send one only when told to; the field states the fit note as a blanket requirement.
review.quote: a fit note (sometimes called a ‘sick note’ or a ‘statement of fitness for work’) if you’ve not been able to work for more than 7 days in a row because of a disability or health condition

review.name: Rate Rebate
review.graph: Must be liable for domestic rates in Northern Ireland.
review.note: The text requires homeowners to be liable, but for tenants either the tenant or the landlord can be liable, so the applicant does not always have to be liable themselves.
review.quote: If you’re a tenant, you or your landlord must be liable for paying the rates.

review.name: Register as a childminder with Ofsted
review.graph: England only. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have separate requirements.
review.note: The guidance is marked as covering England, but the text says nothing about separate requirements in Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.
review.quote: Become a childminder or nanny (England).

review.name: Lasting Power of Attorney
review.graph: Particularly important for those with progressive conditions (dementia, MS, Parkinson's) — must be created while mental capacity remains.
review.note: The text requires mental capacity when making the LPA but never mentions progressive conditions such as dementia, MS or Parkinson's.
review.quote: You must be 18 or over and have mental capacity (the ability to make your own decisions) when you make your LPA .

review.name: Notify OPG of death
review.graph: A registered LPA exists and the donor has died.
review.note: The donor's death is stated as the trigger, but the text does not say the LPA has to be registered for this to apply.
review.quote: OPG will cancel the LPA if the donor dies

review.name: Notify OPG of death
review.graph: Requires a registered LPA to be in place.
review.note: The linked guide is about registered LPAs, but it never says reporting a death requires the LPA to be registered.
review.quote: Using a registered lasting power of attorney (LPA) - attorney duties, starting to act, gifting, ending, revoking an attorney.

review.name: Carer's leave (employer)
review.graph: Must be an employee (not a worker or self-employed). Applies from the first day of employment.
review.note: The carer's leave page confirms employees qualify from day one but never says workers or self-employed people are excluded; that exclusion appears only on the linked parental leave page, which covers a different service.
review.quote: Employees are entitled to carer’s leave from their first day of work for their employer.

review.name: DBS check
review.graph: Role involves working with children or vulnerable adults, or is otherwise in a specified list of eligible positions (healthcare, legal, financial services roles).
review.note: The text mentions children, healthcare and specified positions, but does not mention legal or financial services roles.
review.quote: An exempted question applies when the individual will be working in specific occupations, for certain licenses or specified positions.

review.name: Disabled Persons Railcard
review.graph: Receiving PIP (any component or rate), DLA, Attendance Allowance; or having epilepsy, registered severe visual/hearing impairment, or severe mental or physical disability requiring a companion.
review.note: PIP, Attendance Allowance, epilepsy and visual impairment are stated. DLA qualifies only at certain rates. Hearing impairment needs evidence of deafness or hearing aid use, not registration. No category for severe mental or physical disability requiring a companion exists.
review.quote: I get Personal Independence Payment (PIP) or Adult Disability Payment (ADP) at any rate

review.name: Employers' Liability Insurance
review.graph: Any business employing one or more people under a contract of service or apprenticeship.
review.note: The text says the rule applies once you become an employer, but it never mentions a contract of service or apprenticeship.
review.quote: as soon as you become an employer

review.name: First Homes / Help to Buy scheme
review.graph: First-time buyer purchasing a new-build property through an eligible scheme. For First Homes: property must not exceed £250,000 after discount (£420,000 in London).
review.note: The first-time buyer rule and price caps are stated, but the text does not make new-build a requirement: First Homes can also be a resale bought through an estate agent.
review.quote: New build First Homes cannot cost more £250,000 (or more than £420,000 if the property is in London) after the discount has been applied.

review.name: Right to work check
review.graph: Required for all new employees before they begin work. Employer faces civil penalty if not done.
review.note: The check before employment is stated, but the penalty only applies if the employer also employs an illegal worker, not simply for failing to do the check.
review.quote: You could face a civil penalty if you employ an illegal worker and have not carried out a correct right to work check.

review.name: Right to work check
review.graph: Non-UK/Irish nationals provide a share code via the UK Visas & Immigration online portal. British/Irish citizens present their passport.
review.note: Checking British/Irish passports and using share codes are both stated, but the text never says the online service is run by UK Visas and Immigration, and the share code is only one option.
review.quote: British and Irish citizens cannot get an online share code to prove their right to work. You’ll need to check their original documents - for example, their passport or passport card - or use an identity service provider instead.

review.name: Statutory Redundancy Pay
review.graph: Must have been continuously employed for at least 2 years and been made compulsorily redundant.
review.note: The 2 years' continuous service is supported, but the text does not require compulsory redundancy: people who are laid off or put on short-time working can also qualify.
review.quote: have been dismissed, laid off or put on short-time working - those who opted for early retirement do not qualify

review.name: Student Finance (tuition fee + maintenance loans)
review.graph: Typically 18 or over (no upper age limit for loans, though some conditions apply for those over 60).
review.note: The source says there is no upper age limit for Tuition Fee Loans and that people aged 60 or over get limited Maintenance Loan funding, but it never says applicants are typically 18 or over.
review.quote: There’s no upper age limit for Tuition Fee Loans or grants. If you’re 60 or over You may get limited funding for Maintenance Loans

review.name: Student Finance (tuition fee + maintenance loans)
review.graph: Must be normally resident in England for 3+ years before the course starts, and a UK national or settled person.
review.note: The source requires your home to be in England and 3 years' residence in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man, not 3 years in England specifically; it also includes Irish citizens.
review.quote: your home is in England you’ve been continuously living in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man for 3 years before the first day of your first academic year

review.name: Adult Disability Payment
review.graph: Must have a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability that affects daily living or mobility for at least 13 weeks and is expected to last at least 9 more months.
review.note: The text supports the condition affecting everyday life, but it does not mention the 13-week or 9-month periods.
review.quote: Adult Disability Payment is extra money to help you if you have a disability or long-term health condition that affects your everyday life.

review.name: Carer Support Payment
review.graph: Must live in Scotland.
review.note: The text says carers usually need to live in Scotland, with exceptions for the EU/EEA area with a link to Scotland and for people posted abroad in the Armed Forces or Civil Service, so it is not an absolute rule.
review.quote: Usually, you need to live in Scotland to get carer benefits from Social Security Scotland but you might also be able to apply if:

review.name: Child Disability Payment
review.graph: Child must have a physical or mental disability requiring substantially more care or supervision than a child of the same age, or have difficulty walking.
review.note: The text states physical or mental disability with care, supervision or walking needs, but never compares these with a child of the same age or says 'substantially more'.
review.quote: It's for a child who, because of their physical or mental disability, either: needs help from another person, for much of the day, to manage their bodily functions

review.name: Funeral Support Payment
review.graph: Must be responsible for arranging or paying for a funeral.
review.note: The worked examples pay the person responsible for the funeral, but the text never sets out responsibility for arranging or paying as an eligibility rule.
review.quote: The person who's responsible for the funeral would be able to get a total payment of £1,897.50.

review.name: Funeral Support Payment
review.graph: The funeral must take place in the UK, and applicant must live in Scotland.
review.note: Living in Scotland is stated, but the text never says the funeral must be in the UK; it only limits transport help to travel within the UK.
review.quote: Funeral Support Payment helps pay for funeral costs if you live in Scotland.

review.name: Discretionary Assistance Fund (Wales)
review.graph: EAP: extreme financial hardship or an unexpected crisis with no other money. IAP: must get Income Support, income-based JSA, income-related ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit or Universal Credit, and be leaving an institution, avoiding going into one, setting up home after an unsettled way of life, moving because of relationship breakdown or domestic abuse, or caring for a released prisoner.
review.note: The EAP hardship condition is stated, but the source gives no IAP benefit requirements or qualifying situations, and does not mention having no other money.
review.quote: are experiencing extreme financial hardship have lost your job have applied for benefits and are waiting for your first payment

review.name: Register the death
review.graph: A person has died in England or Wales.
review.note: The page covers deaths in the UK or abroad but never limits the service to deaths in England or Wales, so that restriction is not in the text.
review.quote: Find out how to register a death in the UK or abroad.

review.name: Child Arrangements Order
review.graph: Separated parents with children under 16 (or up to 18 if the order already exists).
review.note: The text says parents who separate can apply for a court order, but it gives no age limit for the child (neither under 16 nor up to 18 if an order already exists), and it also lets other relatives apply.
review.quote: You can apply for a court order if you have parental responsibility . For example, you’re the child’s mother or father.

review.name: Appeal to Immigration Tribunal
review.graph: Must have received a Home Office refusal that explicitly grants a right of appeal.
review.note: The text does require a legal right to appeal, but says you will only 'usually' be told about it in the decision letter, so it does not require the letter to grant the right explicitly; it also covers decisions other than refusals, such as revocation and deportation.
review.quote: You can only appeal to the tribunal if you have the legal right to appeal - you’ll usually be told if you do in your decision letter.

review.name: Statutory Paternity Pay
review.graph: Continuously employed with the same employer for at least 26 weeks and earning at or above the Lower Earnings Limit.
review.note: The text supports the 26 weeks of continuous employment and gives the earnings test as an average of at least £129 a week, but it never mentions the 'Lower Earnings Limit' or links £129 to it, and the field leaves out that the 26 weeks must be reached by the qualifying week.
review.quote: earn an average of at least £129 a week (before tax) give the correct notice have been continuously employed by your employer for at least 26 weeks

review.name: Debt Relief Order (DRO)
review.graph: Must live or have been living in England or Wales.
review.note: The text requires living or working in England and Wales within the last 3 years; the claim leaves out both the working alternative and the 3-year time limit.
review.quote: you’ve lived or worked in England and Wales within the last 3 years

review.name: File annual accounts at Companies House
review.graph: Filed for a UK company by an officer, or by anyone with the company's authentication code such as an accountant. Limited liability partnerships can file only certain package accounts.
review.note: The LLP restriction is stated, and the text says a password and authentication code are needed, but it never says the accounts can be filed by an officer or by anyone holding the authentication code, such as an accountant.
review.quote: Limited liability partnerships can only file certain package accounts using this service.

review.name: Appeal to Tax Tribunal
review.graph: Must have an HMRC decision to appeal. Indirect tax decisions can usually go straight to the tribunal; direct tax decisions must usually be appealed to HMRC first.
review.note: The direct/indirect routing is stated (the text says direct tax 'must' go to HMRC first, with no 'usually'), but the text does not require an HMRC decision: it also allows appeals against decisions by Border Force, the NCA, the WRA and the Gambling Commission.
review.quote: You must appeal direct tax decisions to HMRC before you can appeal to the tribunal. You can usually appeal indirect tax decisions straight to the tribunal.

review.name: Free School Meals
review.graph: Child attends a government-funded school in England (children younger than compulsory school age may also qualify).
review.note: The text mentions a government-funded school only for infant free school meals (reception to year 2), not as a general rule, though it does say children younger than compulsory school age may qualify if the parent gets a qualifying benefit.
review.quote: Your child will be able to get free school meals if they’re in a government-funded school and in: reception class year 1 year 2

review.name: Get a rod fishing licence
review.graph: One licence covers England and Wales, including all of the Border Esk. Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate arrangements.
review.note: The text says a single England and Wales licence is needed, but it excludes the River Tweed, and the claim leaves that exception out.
review.quote: You must have a rod fishing licence for England and Wales if you’re fishing for salmon, trout, freshwater fish, smelt or eel with a rod and line in: England (except the River Tweed) Wales

review.name: Income tax refund (P50)
review.graph: Unemployed for 4 weeks or more, not claiming taxable state benefits, and not returning to work or starting a taxable pension in the same tax year — if you expect to start a new job within 4 weeks, your new employer will make any repayment through your salary instead.
review.note: The page says to check for taxable income, including a works pension, before the end of the tax year, but it does not name 'starting a taxable pension' as an eligibility condition.
review.quote: Check if you get other taxable income or benefits before the end of the tax year — this also includes a works pension from your old employer.
